newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Russian criticises Turkey over Cyprus missiles.
newsitem.headline: Russian criticises Turkey over Cyprus missiles.

text.p: Russia's State Duma Speaker Gennady Seleznyov on Friday criticised Turkish threats to use military force to block the deployment of Russian missiles in Cyprus next year.
"It is blackmail," Seleznyov told a news conference in Nicosia. "Cyprus is not buying nuclear weapons, bacterial or chemical ones. It is just buying a defence system."
Greek Cypriots in the Mediterranean island, divided since a Turkish invasion in 1974, are due to take delivery of the first components of the S-300 surface-to-air missile system next year.
News of the deal, signed in January, prompted warnings from Turkey that it would use military force if necessary to block their deployment.

Turkey invaded Cyprus in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then in power in Greece. Turkey has some 30,000 troops stationed in northern Cyprus and is the only country recognising a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state declared there in 1983.
The Greek Cypriot government in the south is internationally recognised as the island's only government.

"If Cyprus acquires these defence systems it means any country thinking about attacking Cyprus will think about it many times," Seleznyov said. The speaker of Russia's lower house of parliament is on a two-day visit to Cyprus.
International mediation efforts to reunite the island under a federal system have recently gained pace.
The United Nations is engaged in a series of proximity talks between the Greek and Turkish Cypriots to pave the way for direct talks between the two sides by June.
